ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, beneficial owners, and authorized signatories against the Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) sanctions list, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the U.S. OFAC SDN List, and the EU Consolidated List. Additionally, conduct enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons (PEPs) as defined by the FSC, including family members and close associates. Screening must be performed at onboarding and on an ongoing basis, with results documented and retained for at least five years. Any positive match triggers immediate reporting to the FSC and suspension of the formation process. For this reverse logistics entity, the AML risk tier is low, but standard screening protocols apply without exception.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Company Registration and Name Clearance Portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Traditional Chinese. An English name may be registered as a secondary name, but the Chinese name is the legal name. Transliteration must be phonetic, not literal, and must not conflict with existing names. The four-tier naming convention requires: (1) trade name, (2) business type, (3) legal form, and (4) a distinguishing element if necessary. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name application is rejected, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the MOEA within 30 days of the rejection notice. The appeal must include a written statement of reasons, the proposed name, and any supporting evidence. The MOEA will review the appeal and issue a decision within 60 days. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may seek judicial review in the Taipei High Court. The entire process must be completed within the reservation window or the name will be released. It is advisable to consult with a local attorney to prepare the appeal to ensure compliance with procedural requirements.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are permissible in Taiwan, but they are subject to strict scrutiny by tax authorities and banks. For a reverse logistics company, a virtual office may be accepted if it provides a physical address for service of process and mail handling. However, the National Taxation Bureau may require a physical presence for VAT registration and invoice issuance. Banks are likely to reject virtual office addresses for account opening due to AML concerns. It is recommended to have a physical office or a serviced office with a meeting room to satisfy commercial substance requirements and facilitate bank account opening.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) Verify that the registered office is a real, accessible location; (2) Ensure the office is staffed during business hours; (3) Maintain proper records of business activities; (4) Display the company name at the entrance. Risk of unannounced inspection is low to moderate, estimated at 15% within the first year of operation, particularly for logistics and trading entities. The MOEA and tax authorities may conduct on-site visits to confirm commercial substance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act (公司法), Chapter III Limited Company, Articles 98-113 (formation, capital subscription, sole executive director under Article 108) and Article 387 (registration with the central competent authority); Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals (外國人投資條例), Articles 7-13; Regulations Governing Permission for Investment in Taiwan by Mainland Area Investors (大陸地區人民來臺投資許可辦法), Articles 4, 6 and 8; Central Bank Regulations Governing Foreign Exchange Reporting.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Investment Review, Ministry of Economic Affairs (經濟部投資審議司) for investor pre-approval; Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs, and the municipal Department of Economic Development (直轄市政府經濟發展局) for company registration via the MOEA One-Stop Company Registration Portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Company Registration (公司設立登記申請書) supported by the Investment Approval Letter (投資許可函), the bank capital verification certificate (驗資證明), and executed Articles of Incorporation (公司章程).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the amended Company Act; however, the invested capital must be fully remitted from the PRC shareholder into the company's capital escrow account at a licensed Taiwan bank before registration, evidenced by a Central Bank inward-remittance certificate and a CPA capital verification report; release of escrowed funds is permitted only after the company registration certificate is issued.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, that the Company approves the subscription and allotment of its paid-up share capital per the Articles of Incorporation; the shareholder's appointed representative is authorized to remit capital into the Company's escrow account at a licensed Taiwan bank and to execute all incorporation documents.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office at 12F, No. 88, Sec. 2, Dunhua South Road, Da'an District, Taipei City is adopted as the statutory address.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the General Manager, Finance Officer, and Compliance Officer are appointed, authorized to file registration, secure the investment permit, corporate seal, tax ID and customs registrations, and open bank accounts.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that all officers shall operate the reverse-logistics and returned-goods grading business within the approved plan and Taiwan law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Investment Review, Ministry of Economic Affairs (Taiwan) - online investment application portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the investor application with notarized PRC parent-company documents verified by the Straits Exchange Foundation, the reverse-logistics grading business plan (ISIC 5229), the capital-source statement, and a power of attorney naming a Taiwan corporate service agent; pay the NT$10,000 review fee and obtain the positive-list eligibility determination.
required_dossiers: Mainland Area Investor Investment Application Form
PRC parent business license and certificate of incorporation notarized and SEF-verified
Cross-strait outbound-investment lodgment/record certificate of the PRC shareholder
Three-year investment and financial projection for the Taiwan WFOE
Power of attorney to Taiwan representative or agent
Permitted-industry self-declaration under the investment positive list
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to the deficiency (補正) notice within 30 days of receipt and resubmit corrected dossiers; if the application is finally denied, lodge an administrative appeal with the Executive Yuan within 30 days or restructure the shareholding through an eligible corporate vehicle.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Check and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MOEA Company Registration One-Stop Portal (商工行政服務入口網)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the company name check for the Chinese and English names, align the registered business scope with ISIC 5229 reverse logistics, and execute the Articles of Incorporation setting out shareholders, subscribed capital, the sole executive director, and business scope.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Name-conflict rejections are cured by selecting alternate names online in the same session; a substantive denial can be re-filed or appealed to the Department of Commerce within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Taiwan commercial bank and the Central Bank (Taiwan) Foreign Exchange Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a capital collection account in the company's pending-registration name, receive the inward remittance from the PRC shareholder, obtain the Central Bank inward-remittance certificate (匯入匯款證明) and the bank's deposit certificate, and instruct a licensed CPA to issue the capital verification report before registration filing.
required_dossiers: Capital remittance authorization signed by the shareholder
Bank account-opening and anti-money-laundering forms for the pre-registration company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the remittance is returned or rejected, re-present the foreign-exchange application with the Central Bank reporting code; any delayed remittance exceeding the 15-day reporting window requires a written explanation filed with the receiving bank and the Investment Commission.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China; online services through the National Electronic Tax Bureau portal (https://etax.chinatax.gov.cn)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A China-incorporated WFOE receives automatic tax registration through government data sharing between the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and the State Taxation Administration. The competent local tax bureau issues a unified taxpayer identification number (TIN) which serves simultaneously for Enterprise Income Tax, VAT, and export tax refund purposes. No separate VAT registration number is required. The WFOE must file a tax information report and activate its taxpayer profile within 30 days of business license issuance. If a foreign entity has not yet formed a permanent establishment in China, it may obtain a withholding-tax TIN through the Overseas Enterprise Tax Registration procedure before claiming any treaty benefits or zero-rated VAT refunds.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (resident enterprise taxed on worldwide income at 25% Enterprise Income Tax; no pass-through eligibility)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election is available under Chinese tax law. The WFOE is mandatorily classified as a resident enterprise by virtue of incorporation in China. The only relevant election is the voluntary registration by small-scale VAT taxpayers as general VAT taxpayers, which is required for export zero-rating. For income tax purposes no entity classification election exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the VAT Law of the People's Republic of China and its implementing rules, including the general/small-scale taxpayer dual framework and the special VAT invoice system
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 annual taxable sales; exceeding this threshold triggers mandatory registration as a general VAT taxpayer. Below the threshold the WFOE is automatically classified as a small-scale VAT taxpayer (collection rate 3%, temporarily 1%), but can elect general taxpayer status to export and claim zero-rating. All newly incorporated enterprises receive VAT registration automatically regardless of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China operates the Golden Tax Phase IV e-invoicing framework. Full digital electronic invoices (fapiao) are issued via the Electronic Tax Bureau platform or API-connected certified software and are transmitted to the State Taxation Administration in real time. Each invoice carries a unique serial number and a digital electronic seal; no physical fiscal stamping or pre-approval of identical invoice flows is used. The tax authority performs automatic matching between issuing and receiving taxpayers, and VAT filing reconciles output and input invoices with customs and bank data.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from the PRC customs territory qualify for zero-rating, resulting in output VAT at 0% and refund of input VAT. The exporter must be a general VAT taxpayer and must submit a valid customs export declaration. Cross-border services, including international freight forwarding, reverse logistics agency, and offshore processing support services, may qualify for zero-rating if the services are wholly consumed outside China and invoices are issued for foreign-currency collection. Reverse logistics activities physically performed on returned goods inside China, such as inspection, regrading, repair, and repackaging, are generally subject to standard VAT rates unless conducted within a bonded customs supervision zone, in which case applicable bonded policies apply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (出口货物报关单)
VAT Special Invoice for the purchased export goods (增值税专用发票)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill (提单/空运单)
Foreign Exchange Settlement Receipt or Cross-Border RMB Collection Voucher (出口收汇结汇水单/跨境人民币收汇说明)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Tax authorities cross-check export refund claims against customs declarations, logistics bills, insurance records, bank receipts, and FX settlement data. If an export zero-rating claim is found unsupported, fictitious, or misdescribed, the refunded tax is clawed back along with interest from the refund date, and a penalty of 50% to 5 times the tax evaded is imposed under Article 63 of the Law on the Administration of Tax Collection. Criminal liability under Articles 201 or 205 of the Criminal Law may attach to fraudulent VAT refund schemes, leading to fines and imprisonment up to life. Repeated violations trigger disqualification from export tax refund status and adverse credit ranking.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) under the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China operates a bifurcated convertibility framework. The current account is fully convertible for bona fide trade and service transactions, including payments for reverse logistics, freight, and quality inspections, subject to documentary verification and the foreign exchange monitoring system. The capital account, including WFOE registered capital injection, external debt, and cross-border equity transfers, remains restricted and requires case-by-case SAFE registration or approval. Profit remittance is permitted in the current account after submission of tax clearance certificates, audited financial statements, and corporate resolutions; no additional convertibility surcharge applies. For reverse logistics operators, returned-goods proceeds are treated as ordinary current-account receipts and must be matched against import/export customs declarations to avoid audit exceptions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: China does not mandate a statutory surrender ratio for export proceeds. Under the SAFE Goods Trade Foreign Exchange Administration Rules (2012, revised), exporters must repatriate all export proceeds to China (mainland) within 90 days of the export declaration date; thereafter, the proceeds may be held in a foreign-currency current-account deposit or voluntarily converted to RMB at the enterprise's bank. Mandatory verification against the Customs Declaration (export) and the Foreign Exchange Receipts and Payment Declaration Form is required. For reverse logistics goods returned offshore or re-exported, the enterprise must maintain an accurate reconciliation of the original export and subsequent return to avoid currency mismatches and customs-valuation discrepancies.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Airwallex, Payoneer, PingPong) have limited viability as a primary banking rail for a mainland WFOE. Legal constraints: they are not licensed as deposit-taking institutions in China and cannot hold RMB or foreign currency settlement accounts on behalf of a WFOE for capital account transactions. Feasibility rating: Low for capital injection and statutory trade verification; Medium as an auxiliary payment-processing layer for cross-border e-commerce receipts, provided the EMI operates under a Payment Institution License issued by PBOC (as a joint-venture/licensed entity) or serves only as a neutral agent passing funds to a licensed onshore bank. For this reverse logistics scope, Airwallex may be used for small-value refunds and disbursements to offshore suppliers, but must be backed by a compliant onshore corporate bank account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a WFOE opening corporate accounts, physical presence of the legal representative (or a delegated senior officer with a valid notarized power of attorney) is mandatory for the initial KYC interview at the bank's branch. Remote opening or purely video-based onboarding is not permitted for capital escrow accounts. The operational RMB basic account may allow a provisional opening under a video interview followed by physical documentary verification, but the capital account and any foreign-currency current account require in-person signature and biometric verification of the authorized signatories. The bank will conduct at least one face-to-face meeting at the WFOE's registered business address for high-touch foreign-invested entities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership chain involving non-transparent offshore shareholders (e.g., Taiwan-based private owners) and a newly formed WFOE with no prior operating history, triggering heightened due diligence under SAFE and PBOC AML Rules 2023.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a certified group structure chart, shareholders' register, and UBO declaration (Form RC06/RC07) evidencing natural-person ultimate owners; audit-confirmed source of funds of the registered capital; notarized certificates of incorporation of all intermediate holding entities; and an investment commitment letter from the Taiwan parent company.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The reverse logistics business model (ISIC 5229) involves high volumes of returned merchandise, multiple cross-border counterparties, and potential mismatches between goods flow and payment flow, raising suspicion of trade-based money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a complete trade compliance pack containing: master reverse-logistics agreement with offshore clients, sample customs declarations (export and re-import), logistics warehouse receipts, quality-inspection certificates, and a reconciliation ledger matching each batch of returns to the original invoice. Include a written SOP for returned-goods disposal and a 3-year projected cash-flow model to demonstrate economic substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Request to open both a capital escrow account and multiple operational accounts at the same bank may trigger internal fraud and lending-risk questioning, especially if the WFOE has no local payroll or tax registration record.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present the WFOE's business license with unified social credit code, tax registration certificate, office lease agreement, complete Articles of Association, and evidence of local employees enrolled in social insurance. Provide a board resolution authorizing bank signatories and the specific purpose of each account (escrow for capital injection vs. settlement for operations).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border refunds to customers or third-party liquidators may be flagged as anomalous outbound fund transfers under the 'Fully Automatic FX Monitoring and Alert System' if the remittance purpose code is inconsistent.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain a monthly FX purpose-code mapping sheet aligned with SAFE's current-account classification codes (e.g., code '122010' for goods trade refunds). Ensure all refund receipts are supported by original trade contracts, customs declarations of the returned goods, and a written refund policy. Pre-clear large refunds (above USD 50,000 equivalent) with the designated bank relationship manager using a stamped refund justification letter.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The WFOE's registered capital must be remitted from the foreign shareholder via SWIFT MT103/MT202 to the WFOE's Capital Escrow Account (FDI) at a designated Tier-1 bank. The payment must include the precise purpose/reference code required by SAFE: 'Investment in a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise' (FDI registration number). The remitting bank must transmit both the remitter's and beneficiary's full names and account numbers. Upon receipt, the bank performs authenticity verification against the FDI Certificate (received from MOFCOM or now filed with the market regulator) and the Foreign Exchange Business Registration (FDI) Form issued by SAFE. The entire remittance must be registered in the 'Investment Control' module within 15 days of receipt; failure to do so results in funds being blocked and a cross-border red-flag filing. For Taiwan-sourced capital, the cross-strait remittance protocol applies additionally: the Taiwan financial institution must report the remittance to Taiwan's Central Bank (CBC) and ensure it is originated through an approved banking channel to a mainland Chinese bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments for trade settlements (purchase of returned-goods spare parts, freight, overseas warehouse fees) are executed via SWIFT MT103/MT202 from the WFOE's operational RMB/foreign-currency account to the overseas beneficiary. For high-value or recurring disbursements, a Commercial Letter of Credit (LC) issued by an onshore bank can be used when trading with new counterparties; the LC must be backed by an underlying trade contract and the issuing bank will require margin cover of 20–100% depending on creditworthiness. For no-LC transactions, the bank requires a payment instruction with the correct purpose code and supporting documents (contract, invoice, customs declaration if goods are exported/imported). Batch disbursements to multiple logistics providers can be handled via a single payment file uploaded to the bank's treasury interface, but each underlying trade must be verifiable. The ACH (Large-Value Payment System / HVPS) is used for RMB-denominated onshore transfers; cross-border RMB settlement can be routed via SWIFT using RMB, with the benefit of avoiding FX conversion loss but subject to the bank's RMB cross-border clearing approval under SAFE rules.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore CNY forward contracts (deliverable forwards) with a licensed onshore bank, under a rolling real-trade-background documentation requirement (trade contract + customs data) for hedging receivable/payable FX exposure.

CNY non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible for onshore WFOEs due to SAFE regulations; the only permissible NDF market is offshore (CNH), and onshore parties cannot directly participate unless through an approved cross-border interbank channel.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) between CNY and TWD/USD/HKD for long-term liabilities, requiring proof of underlying current-account exposure and SAFE/National Association of Financial Market Institutional Investors (NAFMII) master agreement registration.

FX options (vanilla put/call) with trade-background verification, permissible for hedging import/export cash flows of the reverse logistics operation; premium must be expensed as a financial cost and the option cannot be exercised for speculative gain.

Natural hedging instruments such as maintaining multi-currency cash pools at the same bank (CNY, USD, TWD) and matching inbound and outbound flows to reduce residual FX exposure; but currency conversion between retained foreign exchange and RMB is limited to the actual transaction value with a maximum 10% tolerance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Individual Income Tax Withholding Statement — 各類所得扣繳暨免扣繳憑單申報 (annual withholding return for salaries, directors' fees and service fees)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau (Ministry of Finance, Taiwan)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 January of the following year for the immediately preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of TWD 750–45,000 (approx. USD 23–1,375) under Article 114 of the Income Tax Act, plus recovery of under-withheld tax and interest; continued default triggers collection enforcement and compulsory deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business Tax (VAT) Return — 營業稅申報 (January–February filing node of the recurring bi-monthly cycle)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau (Ministry of Finance, Taiwan)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Each two-month VAT period filed by the 15th day of the following month; annual-cycle anchor: January–February return due 15 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of TWD 3,000–30,000 (approx. USD 92–915) per return, plus 1% late-payment surcharge for every two days of delay up to 15%; chronic non-filing risks business registration revocation and compulsory striking-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Effective Beneficial Owner (UBO) Annual Confirmation — 有效財務受益人年度確認申報
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Company Registration Authority (Trade and Business Portal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March (confirmation window 1–31 March); also due within 14 days of any shareholding transfer during the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: MOEA notice-to-remedy followed by administrative fine of TWD 50,000–500,000 (approx. USD 1,525–15,250) under the Money Laundering Control Act; persistent default risks compulsory deregistration by MOEA.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Annual Settlement Return — 營利事業所得稅結算申報
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau (Ministry of Finance, Taiwan)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing season 1–31 May for the prior fiscal year; automatic extension to 30 June for CPA-attested e-filings
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 3% of unpaid tax if filed within 10 days of notice, or 10% thereafter, plus 1% monthly interest on unpaid tax; continued non-compliance triggers collection actions, asset attachment and subsequent compulsory deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements Approval and Shareholders' Resolution Record — 年度決算書表承認及股東決議記錄
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Retained at the registered office in Taiwan; filed with MOEA Commercial Administration Office only upon Article 20 Company Act demand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' approval completed within 6 months after fiscal year end (by 30 June); resolution records and minutes kept permanently
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Responsible person subject to fine of TWD 10,000–50,000 (approx. USD 305–1,525) for non-production of final accounts; repeated non-compliance after MOEA order triggers compulsory deregistration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Company Act Article 20 (MOEA 2019 order), mandatory CPA audit and certification is required where paid-in capital exceeds TWD 30 million; additionally, a CPA-attested financial statement must accompany the annual income tax return where annual operating revenue exceeds TWD 100 million or the enterprise uses Blue Return status. Companies below these thresholds may file internally prepared financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Business Entity Accounting Act (商業會計法) with Taiwan Local GAAP (Enterprise Accounting Standard No. 1 for private enterprises); Taiwan-IFRS mandatory only for listed and public-interest companies. Functional reporting currency: TWD, with USD translation permitted for bookkeeping.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A WFOE must register its effective financial beneficiaries with MOEA at incorporation and within 14 days of every shareholding transfer. Annually, the register must be re-confirmed in the fixed 1–31 March window; the confirmation requires current shareholding percentages, directors' and shareholders' identity data, and PEP/criminal-history declarations. Any unregistered share transfer is ineffective against the company and exposes the company to MOEA fines.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500–1,500 per year (registered address plus corporate secretarial/記帳士 service in Taipei, Taichung or Kaohsiung; excludes event-driven filing fees for capital changes)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500–5,000 per year (full CPA audit and certification for a small WFOE; reduced US$1,000–2,000 for a CPA-reviewed financial statement where audit thresholds are not met)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% preferential rate for High and New Technology Enterprises (HNTE) certified under the PRC Administrative Measures; 10% rate for key integrated circuit enterprises; additional 75-100% super deduction for qualifying R&D expenses (effective rate can fall below 15%)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Quarterly Enterprise Income Tax Prepayment Return (Form A201010) filed through the Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Taxation, 电子税务局)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 15 calendar days after the end of each quarter (March 31, June 30, September 30, December 31)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total operating income including reverse logistics fees, returned-goods grading commissions, and ancillary disposal revenue
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident investors should ensure only PRC-source revenue is reported; cross-border service income must be allocated per the Permanent Establishment (PE) determination

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs of processing returns: inbound freight, repair/remanufacturing inputs, grading labor, warehouse overheads
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cost reimbursement to overseas affiliates must be supported by arm's length invoices and TP evidence; non-resident payers must withhold on any deemed China-source services

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Management and operational costs, excluding non-deductible items such as VAT paid, penalties, and bribes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocated head office or parent company charges must pass the beneficial expense test; online filing of deduction schedules with APAs is recommended

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: For WFOE residents, taxable income after adjustments, loss offsets, and related-party adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident on actual profit method may use a deemed profit rate for Chinese-source income; TP margins must be substantiated

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prepaid corporate income tax at 25% (or 15% for HNTE) on quarterly cumulative taxable income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the standard conversion rate for foreign currency income; prepayments are credited against the annual return

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment surcharge of 0.05% per day on unpaid tax; late filing fine of RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000, increased to RMB 2,000 to RMB 50,000 for repeated and serious violations

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Enterprise Income Tax Return (Form A, A100000) with coordinated schedules (A101010-A108000) submitted through e-Taxation
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 5 months of fiscal year-end (May 31 for a calendar-year WFOE), including the annual audit adjustment package and related-party transaction reporting

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross turnover from reverse logistics services: process fees, inspection/grading fees, and resale of returned goods
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident contracting party must exclude revenue from offshore sales of goods unless attributable to a service PE in China

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of returned goods acquired, inbound/outbound shipping, repair materials, and third-party logistics charges
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany purchase prices must be consistent with the CUP or TNMM; retain customs and warehouse documentation

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible expenses, entertainment overlimitation, advertising cap, interest limitation, and related-party TP adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident investors, any adjustment increasing foreign-related revenue must be recorded through supplementary taxable income schedules

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Qualifying dividends from Chinese resident companies and government grants, with certificate requirements
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not applicable to non-resident withholding tax; however, treaty exemption may be claimed on foreign passive income with TRC

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total CIT liability after all credits, quarterly prepayments, and foreign-tax credits; represents the annual reconciliation figure
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Withholding liabilities on dividends, interest, royalties paid to Taiwanese residents are separate and reported under the non-resident withholding monthly return

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Underpayment due to misstatement: 50% to 500% of the tax evaded; non-filing: fine up to RMB 50,000 and daily surcharge of 0.05%; criminal referral if evaded tax exceeds RMB 50,000 and represents more than 10% of tax payable

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% under PRC Corporate Income Tax Law (Article 3) for dividends paid to non-resident enterprises; reduced to 5% under the Cross-Strait Double Taxation Agreement granted by China to a Taiwanese resident company that beneficially owns at least 25% of the WFOE's capital
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Taiwanese investor must obtain a valid Taiwan Tax Resident Certificate (TRC) from the Taiwan tax authority. Prior to dividend distribution, the WFOE (as withholding agent) must file an Application for Non-Resident Treaty Reduced Withholding (Stamp) with the PRC competent tax bureau, attaching the TRC, beneficial ownership declaration, shareholding certificate, and an undertaking to report material changes. The reduced rate applies only where the investor is the ultimate beneficial owner with economic substance in Taiwan; approval normally issues within 30 days.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory rates: 10% withholding on interest and royalties paid to non-residents. Under the Cross-Strait Double Taxation Agreement, the applicable ceiling is 7% for royalties and 7% for interest, provided the recipient is the beneficial owner and a Taiwanese tax resident.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File (contemporaneous documentation) is mandatory for one fiscal year where annual related-party transactions exceed RMB 200,000,000 for tangible goods, RMB 100,000,000 for intangible asset transfers, service transactions, or financial transactions. Master File is required when the global consolidated revenue of the group exceeds RMB 5,000,000,000. The related-party transaction reporting schedule (A105050) is compulsory for all WFOEs regardless of threshold and must be filed with the annual CIT return.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China applies a General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) under CIT Article 47 and the Special Tax Adjustment Regulations (SAT Notice No. 16, 2009). Although no standalone Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) exists, a Taiwanese investor claiming treaty benefits must demonstrate substantial business activity in Taiwan — real employees, premises, decision-making, and risk assumption. A shell investor without substance will be denied treaty reductions and may face recharacterisation of income; the WFOE’s own substance is evaluated to ensure it is not a conduit deriving improper non-resident tax advantages.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilfully underreporting reverse-logistics service revenue, fabricating returned-goods inventory, or inflating related-party costs without economic reality
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil restitution of tax evaded plus a fine of 50% to 500% of the evaded amount; criminal prosecution under PRC Criminal Law (Article 201) if the evaded tax exceeds RMB 50,000 and constitutes more than 10% of the tax due, carrying up to 7 years’ imprisonment and additional fines
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and legal representatives may be jointly and severally liable for restitution, subjected to personal asset freezing, exit restrictions (travel bans), and, in flagrant cases, criminal detention and imprisonment; corporate veil will be pierced where the company is a mere alter ego of the Taiwanese investor

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Registering a Taiwanese investment vehicle with no commercial activity, no local management, no employees, and no substantive decision-making, used solely to claim the 5% Cross-Strait treaty dividend rate
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty reduction resulting in re-withholding at 10% domestic rate; imposition of GAAR adjustment with a 10-30% surcharge on the re-adjusted tax payable; potential 0.05% daily interest on under-withheld tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for failure to withhold correctly; travel bans and asset seizure for the responsible foreign investor; criminal exposure if the shell arrangement facilitates money laundering

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare or submit contemporaneous Local File/Master File, applying a non-arm's length margin to related-party reverse logistics fees, or failing to report cross-border transactions on schedule A105050
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Mandatory TP adjustment to an arm's length result; assessment of interest at the benchmark loan rate plus 5 percentage points; penalty of 0.05% daily on the underpaid CIT; fine up to RMB 50,000 for missing documentation; criminal referral for deliberate falsification
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Executives who sign false TP declarations or knowingly submit inaccurate documentation may incur civil joint liability, criminal sanctions for invoice and financial misreporting, and exit restrictions pending full payment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating cross-border reverse logistics payment flows through unstructured local ACH or Airwallex rails without implementing AML/KYC procedures, or processed through undisclosed shell accounts to evade tax verification
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law, fines up to RMB 5,000,000 for a corporate violator, suspension of business license, revocation of payment licenses; where funds derive from predicate offences, criminal liability for money laundering (imprisonment up to 10 years plus fines)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally fined up to RMB 500,000, prohibited from banking management duties, and criminally prosecuted for knowing participation in illicit payment transfers; travel bans apply until the AML investigation concludes
